validated_report:
Electricity use over time is measured in Watthours
Watts measure power at a specific moment, but we use Watthours (Wh) to measure how much electricity is used over a period of time.
One Watthour is the energy of one Watt used for one hour.
For example, if you use a 40-Watt (0.04 kW) light bulb for five hours, you have used 200 Wh, or 0.2 kWh, of electrical energy.
